passages: Hyperliquid whales, the exchange’s largest Bitcoin ( CRYPTO: BTC ) traders, have made a major strategic shift, going net short on Bitcoin for the first time in seven months.

According to on-chain analytics firm Glassnode, which reported the shift, these whales moved from a net long position to a net short one, and their current short position is the largest since October 2025.
Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most.
His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.
However, the whales had more success in October 2025 when they last held a similar level of short exposure.
Bitcoin peaked at $126,080 on October 6, 2025, closed the month at $109,567, then slid 22.7% to $84,676 by November 22, 2025.
Traders closely monitor these whales due to their substantial financial backing and potential access to better information, though their track record is mixed.
For instance, they last went net short in March and then rebuilt their long positions during Bitcoin’s April rally.
From April 12 to May 10, Bitcoin surged 16.1%, rising from $70,661 to $82,018 and catching many short traders off guard.
Glassnode tracks only one exchange, leaving gaps in its analysis.

A whale might own Bitcoin stored in cold storage, on a centralized exchange, or through an ETF and could short on Hyperliquid to protect their assets without selling, which would still count as a bearish position in Glassnode’s data.
So, are the Hyperliquid whales predicting a further drop in Bitcoin’s price, or just hedging their existing holdings elsewhere?
Bitcoin's last five-week slide ended in two very different ways, and ETF outflows, whale shorts, and a key moving average now complicate the comparison.
Funding rates also provide insight into market sentiment.
These rates are the periodic fees that help align perpetual futures prices with the spot price.
On November 7, Binance’s funding rate was slightly positive, at 0.0000059, suggesting that the broader market isn’t heavily positioned for a price drop.
Are they hedging a hidden stash or sniffing out the next leg down?
Bitcoin traded around $75,662 on November 8, down 8% over the past 30 days and just under its lowest 30-day close of $75,775 on November 6.
Hyperliquid traders held $612 million in leveraged long positions just a week earlier, on November 2, showing a drastic shift in strategy.
These trades are recorded on Hyperliquid’s public blockchain, enabling Glassnode to analyze the holdings of significant accounts.
In May 2026, they reached a high level of net longs, but Bitcoin subsequently dropped by 28.6% to $58,566 by June 30.
Additionally, most Bitcoin transactions occur on exchange order books that don’t interact with the blockchain, which is why significant whale buying in October did not lead to price increases.
Open interest data indicates a directional bias among traders.
Hyperliquid represents only a small fraction of the total futures market.
A week of net ETF inflows that surpasses the $1.28 billion that departed in the week ending November 6 could undercut the whales’ short.

If Bitcoin continues to drop, these long positions could face liquidation, an automatic closure of a borrowed position when losses exceed the initial deposit, adding selling pressure in favor of the whales.

The company’s dividend cushion is its dollar reserve, reported at $4.79 billion in the November 2 filing. Management has described the reserve as a way to keep paying dividends and interest through market swings, including periods when raising capital is costly. According to its third-quarter report, USD assets of $5.07 billion cover 3.4 years of dividend and interest obligations, while preferred dividends in that quarter alone totaled $419.56 million.

To help ease the load, Strategy has sold $432 million worth of Bitcoin in 2026, tying those sales to preferred dividends and STRC buybacks. The legacy software business from the MicroStrategy days contributed $125.43 million in third-quarter revenue, with subscription services adding $68.59 million. Software sales alone are not enough to cover a single quarter of preferred dividends.

Strategy uses fair value accounting for its Bitcoin, meaning any price change, up or down, hits the company’s financials each quarter, whether or not the coins are sold. If Bitcoin ends a quarter below $75,451, the whole position would show an unrealized loss, a paper loss on assets still held. For every $1,000 Bitcoin falls below that line, Strategy would book roughly $849 million of paper losses.

Shareholders know how drastic these swings can be. Strategy reported an unrealized loss of $14.46 billion on its digital assets in the first quarter of 2026, followed by an $8.32 billion loss in the second quarter, then a $20.91 billion gain in the third quarter, producing earnings per share of $44.75.

Management has said a drop in Bitcoin’s price below Strategy’s average purchase cost triggers no contractual consequences. CEO Phong Le said during the February 5 earnings call that the company has no covenants or triggers that require action if Bitcoin falls below that price, and that it plans to stick to its strategy.

If Bitcoin closes below $75,451, MSTR’s valuation would likely face significant pressure. Strategy’s mNAV, its market value divided by the value of its Bitcoin, is around 1.12, a slim premium. If that premium narrows toward 1, selling new MSTR shares to buy Bitcoin could stop adding Bitcoin per share, choking the funding engine behind the whole model.

Upcoming events could also move MSTR before Bitcoin makes any significant move. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor has posted “Connecting the dots” with his Bitcoin tracking chart, a pattern that has preceded purchase filings the next business day, which points to a possible 8-K on November 9. However, the post names no amount, and a purchase funded by shares sold around 1.12 mNAV would add little Bitcoin per share.

MSCI ( NYSE: MSCI ) is also scheduled to rule on Strategy on November 11. Index funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, or 3.1% of the company, so a removal could force those funds to sell. Strategy has argued that index providers should focus on measuring markets and leave asset decisions to companies.

A Bitcoin close below Strategy’s average cost of $75,451 could hit MSTR’s earnings and investor sentiment far harder than it moves Bitcoin. For MSTR holders, the cost line feeds the quarterly loss, the 1.12 premium, and MSCI’s review all at once. For Bitcoin, it’s an accounting figure other holders can ignore, and the coin trades below its 20-day and 50-day moving averages of $79,362 and $81,889 but above its 200-day average of $73,194.

If Bitcoin holds above $75,451 and MSCI keeps Strategy on November 11, MSTR could claw back some of its 2026 losses. If Bitcoin closes below cost and MSCI drops the stock, MSTR might face forced index selling on top of a smaller premium. STRC is the clearest signal, since holding $100 shows the market still trusts the dividend engine, while a slide well under $99.84 would show that trust fading.

extraction.body: Bitcoin's last five-week slide ended in two very different ways, and ETF outflows, whale shorts, and a key moving average now complicate the comparison. Which history is this selloff repeating? This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them. Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ) is on course for its fifth week of losses in a row, marking a Bitcoin losing streak that began in early October. It trades at around $75,662, which is down roughly 3.3% from last week’s close and about 40% below its all-time high of $126,080 recorded on October 6, 2025. Over the past four weeks, each week closed lower than the one before. Bitcoin started at $86,507 on October 4 and dropped to $78,231 by November 1, culminating in a 2.28% loss that last week. Bitcoin’s last losing streak this long ended on March 1. So, what followed that Bitcoin losing streak, and does the current situation resemble it? Spot Bitcoin ETFs, which are funds that hold Bitcoin and trade on stock exchanges like regular stocks, saw significant outflows totaling $1.28 billion in the week ending November 6. When investors pull out more ETF shares than they purchase, the funds must sell Bitcoin, turning a consistent buyer into a seller. According to SoSoValue, four out of the five trading days in that week saw money leave the funds, including outflows of $398.6 million on November 2, $430.2 million on November 5, and $411.9 million on November 6. The only day with net inflows was November 4, when the funds took in $74.6 million. On November 6, Bitcoin closed at $75,775, marking its lowest closing price in the past month amid heavy ETF selling for two consecutive days. This trend of selling started earlier, with the funds reporting a $643.3 million outflow on October 30, the largest one-day exit since at least October 9. The flow of money and the price movement often affect each other. When prices fall, ETF holders may feel compelled to sell, further driving prices down. Additionally, Bitcoin’s weekly trading volume has increased over the past three weeks leading up to November 8, indicating that sellers are becoming more active as the price continues to drop. Extended losing streaks are uncommon for Bitcoin. Even during the downturn in 2018, when Bitcoin closed as low as $3,217 on December 16, it never experienced more than three consecutive losing weeks. The two most recent streaks lasting five weeks or longer ended in very different situations. In early 2026, Bitcoin faced six weeks of losses, dropping from $93,634 on January 18 to $65,769 on March 1, with a low of $60,001 reached in the week ending February 8. Four weeks later, on March 29, it closed at $65,957, nearly unchanged. By eight weeks after the streak ended, it rose to $78,674 on April 26, a gain of about 20% from the end of the losing streak. In contrast, the 2022 streak also lasted six weeks, dropping from $39,678 on April 17, 2022, to $29,446 on May 29. Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ) is on course for its fifth week of losses in a row, marking a Bitcoin losing streak that began in early October. It trades at around $75,662, which is down roughly 3.3% from last week’s close and about 40% below its all-time high of $126,080 recorded on October 6, 2025.

Over the past four weeks, each week closed lower than the one before. Bitcoin started at $86,507 on October 4 and dropped to $78,231 by November 1, culminating in a 2.28% loss that last week. Bitcoin’s last losing streak this long ended on March 1. So, what followed that Bitcoin losing streak, and does the current situation resemble it?

Spot Bitcoin ETFs, which are funds that hold Bitcoin and trade on stock exchanges like regular stocks, saw significant outflows totaling $1.28 billion in the week ending November 6. When investors pull out more ETF shares than they purchase, the funds must sell Bitcoin, turning a consistent buyer into a seller.

According to SoSoValue, four out of the five trading days in that week saw money leave the funds, including outflows of $398.6 million on November 2, $430.2 million on November 5, and $411.9 million on November 6. The only day with net inflows was November 4, when the funds took in $74.6 million.

On November 6, Bitcoin closed at $75,775, marking its lowest closing price in the past month amid heavy ETF selling for two consecutive days. This trend of selling started earlier, with the funds reporting a $643.3 million outflow on October 30, the largest one-day exit since at least October 9.

The flow of money and the price movement often affect each other. When prices fall, ETF holders may feel compelled to sell, further driving prices down. Additionally, Bitcoin’s weekly trading volume has increased over the past three weeks leading up to November 8, indicating that sellers are becoming more active as the price continues to drop.

Extended losing streaks are uncommon for Bitcoin. Even during the downturn in 2018, when Bitcoin closed as low as $3,217 on December 16, it never experienced more than three consecutive losing weeks. The two most recent streaks lasting five weeks or longer ended in very different situations.

In early 2026, Bitcoin faced six weeks of losses, dropping from $93,634 on January 18 to $65,769 on March 1, with a low of $60,001 reached in the week ending February 8. Four weeks later, on March 29, it closed at $65,957, nearly unchanged. By eight weeks after the streak ended, it rose to $78,674 on April 26, a gain of about 20% from the end of the losing streak.

In contrast, the 2022 streak also lasted six weeks, dropping from $39,678 on April 17, 2022, to $29,446 on May 29. Four weeks later, Bitcoin fell to $21,029 on June 26, then dipped to $19,310 on July 3, and by eight weeks out, it had only slightly rebounded to close at $22,601 on July 24, still significantly lower than where the losing streak concluded.

Neither of these situations marked a lasting recovery. The rebound from the spring 2026 drop eventually faded, leading to Bitcoin’s lowest close in a year at $58,566 on June 30. Additionally, the presence of ETFs changes the comparison to 2022 since U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had not yet launched at that time. Now, Bitcoin has a new set of buyers due to these ETFs, but they have also contributed to the current sell-off.

Moreover, large traders have shifted their stance regarding Bitcoin. On-chain analytics firm Glassnode noted that major traders on Hyperliquid began to take net short positions on October 27, after holding long positions for seven months, and have continued to add to those shorts. A short position profits when prices fall, indicating that they expect further declines.

A quick recovery from this downturn appears unlikely. In previous long losing streaks, it took at least a month to find a floor, and so far, there has been no sign of returning buyers in the market. To avoid a fifth consecutive loss, Bitcoin will need a significant shift in buying sentiment.

extraction.body: Three officers from the departmental police unit (UDMO ) were killed on July 22 in an ambush by the Gran Grif gang in Liancourt. Days earlier, nine civilians were massacred in L'Estère by the Kokorat San Ras gang. The gang’s notorious leader, Fadens “Meyè” Tilus, was later killed by a self-defense group. Residents continue to denounce government inaction as violence intensifies in the Artibonite region. GONAÏVES — At least three officers from the Departmental Law Enforcement Unit (UDMO) were killed on Tuesday, July 22, during an operation in Liancourt—a commune in the lower Artibonite—when their armored vehicle was ambushed and burned by members of the Gran Grif gang. In a separate attack, armed men from Kokorat San Ras, whose leader was killed by a local self-defense brigade, stormed the neighboring Kanpenyen community in L’Estère and murdered at least nine people. These incidents highlight the latest wave of ongoing violence in the region. These police officers, identified by the authorities as Jean Louis Daniel, Dareus Daniel and Fegensly Mertus, distressed, spent hours waiting for reinforcements that never arrived. “We have received information that the police officers were the victims of a criminal act carried out by members of the Gran Grif gang,” Féquière Casséus, spokesperson for the Haitian National Police (PNH) in Artibonite, told The Haitian Times . “We are still compiling the reports before releasing more details.” The Gran Grif gang—designated a terrorist organization earlier this year by the Trump administration— is one of the most feared armed groups in the region. It has been the target of ongoing police operations aimed at reclaiming control of Savien and Liancourt, two communes that have been occupied since as early as 2018. Videos circulating on social media showed the aftermath of the ambush—an immobilized armored police vehicle in flames and the bodies of the slain officers being desecrated by men waving red handkerchiefs. These latest killings echo a 2023 incident in which seven UDMO agents were slain at the Liancourt police station. The attacks have reignited criticism over the government’s failure to curb gang violence and adequately equip the police. “There is no genuine will to combat the armed groups that operate with impunity,” said André Saint-Louis, coordinator of the human rights organization—Committee for Peace Initiative in the Lower Artibonite (KILBA). “The Presidential Transitional Council [CPT] remains inactive and appears unconcerned about the dire situation facing the Haitian people.” “There is no genuine will to combat the armed groups that operate with impunity in the department.” The Minister of Economy and Finance (MEF), Patrick Pélissier, confirmed that on July 18 he disbursed 117,130,000 gourdes, or about $901,000, to mobilize the necessary resources for the PNH’s anti-gang operations. Saint-Louis said the number of officers killed in clashes with Gran Grif in recent days may be as high as four. He added that eight weapons were seized and one armored vehicle torched in the ambush. “The fallen officers were deployed in deplorable conditions, without adequate ammunition or proper equipment,” he said. In addition to Liancourt and L’Estère, other areas in the region like Pont-Sondé, Gros-Morne, Verrettes, Petite-Rivière de l’Artibonite and La Chapelle have been especially affected by rampant gang violence, with residents being consistently killed, kidnapped, extorted or forced to flee their homes. Just days earlier, July 17 to 18, another deadly incident unfolded in Kanpenyen—a community in L’Estère, where members of the Kokorat San Ras gang killed nine civilians. The attack, reportedly in retaliation, came shortly before the gang’s notorious leader, Fadens “Meyè” Tilus, was killed by an armed self-defense group known as the “Coalition.” A source with insider information confirmed Tilus’ death to The Haitian Times , though police officials have not verified it. “We treat this information with the utmost seriousness, but at this time we cannot confirm whether the gang leader has been killed,” said Casseus, PNH spokesperson. The victims in Kapenyen were described as peaceful residents, mostly engaged in agriculture. Their identities have not yet been released. Local authorities said more information will be shared at a forthcoming press briefing in Gonaïves. Government Commissioner Guiverna Guillaume said he, too, learned of the massacre through the media. “We are collaborating with police forces to clarify what happened and restore security in the jurisdiction of Gonaïves,” he told The Haitian Times . In the wake of the violence, the Committee for Demobilization Against Gangs and Insecurity in Artibonite announced new mobilizations against the government’s inaction. The group’s spokesperson, Jécosiasse Pierre, condemned the killings in Kapenyen and demanded the removal of Artibonite’s top police official. “We demand the immediate resignation of Commissioner Kalerb Exantus,” Pierre said. “His inefficiency has only enabled the rise in insecurity.” Pierre also said National Road No. 1 would remain blocked in L’Estère, where supporters of Kokorat San Ras have disrupted traffic. Residents fleeing Kapenyen were seen arriving in Gonaïves with small bags and children in tow, seeking shelter from the violence. passages: Haitian security forces have intensified operations against armed gangs, killing a notorious gang leader in a series of coordinated attacks involving explosive drones as authorities push to reclaim territory controlled by criminal groups.
Caribbean National Weekly — your trusted source for Caribbean news, culture, and community across the diaspora.
Haitian police said Saintil died from multiple gunshot wounds sustained during a security operation.
However, the National Human Rights Defense Network (RNDDH) reported that he was critically injured Thursday night when an explosive drone struck his vehicle and died the following day.

The operations form part of an intensified campaign by Haitian authorities and international security partners to weaken armed gangs and restore government control over communities affected by years of violence.

In a recent national address, he pledged that the Haitian state would not surrender territory to armed groups and insisted that security operations would continue until public order and state authority were restored.
The organization has called attention to reports of civilian casualties as security forces increasingly rely on drone strikes to target gang leaders and their strongholds.
“One less gang leader,” Fils-Aimé declared on social media, reaffirming his government's commitment to dismantling the armed groups responsible for widespread violence and instability across Haiti.
The prime minister has also emphasized that operations must comply with Haitian law and international human rights obligations.

The latest offensive comes amid an expanded international security presence in Haiti, including the deployment of approximately 2,500 Salvadoran troops following the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians during a gang ambush in October.
Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé confirmed the death of Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang operating in the densely populated Cité Soleil neighborhood of Port-au-Prince.
According to the human rights organization, at least seven explosive drones were deployed during coordinated operations targeting several gang-controlled communities.
Haitian police subsequently recovered the burned-out vehicle in the Santo district of Croix-des-Bouquets, but the four men remain missing.

Authorities have maintained that their objective is to dismantle criminal networks, regain control of gang-held communities and create the security conditions necessary for Haiti's long-awaited elections.

Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé confirmed the death of Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang operating in the densely populated Cité Soleil neighborhood of Port-au-Prince. “One less gang leader,” Fils-Aimé declared on social media, reaffirming his government's commitment to dismantling the armed groups responsible for widespread violence and instability across Haiti. Saintil's gang is affiliated with the powerful Viv Ansanm coalition, an alliance of armed groups that controls significant portions of the capital and has expanded its influence into other regions of the country. Haitian police said Saintil died from multiple gunshot wounds sustained during a security operation. However, the National Human Rights Defense Network (RNDDH) reported that he was critically injured Thursday night when an explosive drone struck his vehicle and died the following day. According to the human rights organization, at least seven explosive drones were deployed during coordinated operations targeting several gang-controlled communities. The RNDDH reported that five gang members were killed and approximately 15 others injured in the attack targeting Saintil, while additional casualties were recorded during separate confrontations. The operations form part of an intensified campaign by Haitian authorities and international security partners to weaken armed gangs and restore government control over communities affected by years of violence. Security forces have also targeted Wilson Joseph, leader of the notorious 400 Mawozo gang, which has been linked to kidnappings and other violent crimes. Joseph's home was reportedly bombed during a recent operation, although he is believed to have survived the attack and gone into hiding. Haitian police subsequently recovered the burned-out vehicle in the Santo district of Croix-des-Bouquets, but the four men remain missing. The incident has heightened tensions and prompted additional security operations targeting armed groups suspected of involvement in the attack. Meanwhile, the RNDDH has raised concerns about the potential impact of explosive drone operations on civilians living in densely populated neighborhoods. The organization has called attention to reports of civilian casualties as security forces increasingly rely on drone strikes to target gang leaders and their strongholds. Haiti has experienced years of escalating gang violence, with armed groups controlling major roads, neighborhoods and commercial routes, particularly in and around Port-au-Prince. The violence has forced hundreds of thousands of residents to flee their homes, disrupted essential services and severely restricted access to food, healthcare and humanitarian assistance. The prime minister has also emphasized that operations must comply with Haitian law and international human rights obligations. Despite the intensified offensive, questions remain about coordination among Haiti's police, military and international security partners, as well as the effectiveness of drone strikes in reducing gang violence without placing civilians at further risk. Authorities have maintained that their objective is to dismantle criminal networks, regain control of gang-held communities and create the security conditions necessary for Haiti's long-awaited elections. coreStoryFacts.text: “We have received information that the police officers were the victims of a criminal act carried out by members of the Gran Grif gang,” Féquière Casséus, spokesperson for the Haitian National Police (PNH) in Artibonite, told The Haitian Times .
Days earlier, nine civilians were massacred in L'Estère by the Kokorat San Ras gang.
The gang’s notorious leader, Fadens “Meyè” Tilus, was later killed by a self-defense group.
Residents continue to denounce government inaction as violence intensifies in the Artibonite region.
“We treat this information with the utmost seriousness, but at this time we cannot confirm whether the gang leader has been killed,” said Casseus, PNH spokesperson.
Government Commissioner Guiverna Guillaume said he, too, learned of the massacre through the media.
The group’s spokesperson, Jécosiasse Pierre, condemned the killings in Kapenyen and demanded the removal of Artibonite’s top police official.
These incidents highlight the latest wave of ongoing violence in the region.
The attacks have reignited criticism over the government’s failure to curb gang violence and adequately equip the police.

Videos circulating on social media showed the aftermath of the ambush—an immobilized armored police vehicle in flames and the bodies of the slain officers being desecrated by men waving red handkerchiefs.
These police officers, identified by the authorities as Jean Louis Daniel, Dareus Daniel and Fegensly Mertus, distressed, spent hours waiting for reinforcements that never arrived.
Saint-Louis said the number of officers killed in clashes with Gran Grif in recent days may be as high as four.

The Minister of Economy and Finance (MEF), Patrick Pélissier, confirmed that on July 18 he disbursed 117,130,000 gourdes, or about $901,000, to mobilize the necessary resources for the PNH’s anti-gang operations.

extraction.body: Three officers from the departmental police unit (UDMO ) were killed on July 22 in an ambush by the Gran Grif gang in Liancourt. Days earlier, nine civilians were massacred in L'Estère by the Kokorat San Ras gang. The gang’s notorious leader, Fadens “Meyè” Tilus, was later killed by a self-defense group. Residents continue to denounce government inaction as violence intensifies in the Artibonite region. GONAÏVES — At least three officers from the Departmental Law Enforcement Unit (UDMO) were killed on Tuesday, July 22, during an operation in Liancourt—a commune in the lower Artibonite—when their armored vehicle was ambushed and burned by members of the Gran Grif gang. “We demand the immediate resignation of Commissioner Kalerb Exantus,” Pierre said. “His inefficiency has only enabled the rise in insecurity.”

Pierre also said National Road No. 1 would remain blocked in L’Estère, where supporters of Kokorat San Ras have disrupted traffic. Residents fleeing Kapenyen were seen arriving in Gonaïves with small bags and children in tow, seeking shelter from the violence.

passages: Haitian security forces have intensified operations against armed gangs, killing a notorious gang leader in a series of coordinated attacks involving explosive drones as authorities push to reclaim territory controlled by criminal groups.
Caribbean National Weekly — your trusted source for Caribbean news, culture, and community across the diaspora.
Haitian police said Saintil died from multiple gunshot wounds sustained during a security operation.
However, the National Human Rights Defense Network (RNDDH) reported that he was critically injured Thursday night when an explosive drone struck his vehicle and died the following day.

The operations form part of an intensified campaign by Haitian authorities and international security partners to weaken armed gangs and restore government control over communities affected by years of violence.

In a recent national address, he pledged that the Haitian state would not surrender territory to armed groups and insisted that security operations would continue until public order and state authority were restored.
The organization has called attention to reports of civilian casualties as security forces increasingly rely on drone strikes to target gang leaders and their strongholds.
“One less gang leader,” Fils-Aimé declared on social media, reaffirming his government's commitment to dismantling the armed groups responsible for widespread violence and instability across Haiti.
The prime minister has also emphasized that operations must comply with Haitian law and international human rights obligations.

The latest offensive comes amid an expanded international security presence in Haiti, including the deployment of approximately 2,500 Salvadoran troops following the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians during a gang ambush in October.
Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé confirmed the death of Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang operating in the densely populated Cité Soleil neighborhood of Port-au-Prince.
According to the human rights organization, at least seven explosive drones were deployed during coordinated operations targeting several gang-controlled communities.
Haitian police subsequently recovered the burned-out vehicle in the Santo district of Croix-des-Bouquets, but the four men remain missing.

Authorities have maintained that their objective is to dismantle criminal networks, regain control of gang-held communities and create the security conditions necessary for Haiti's long-awaited elections.

extraction.body: Haitian security forces have intensified operations against armed gangs, killing a notorious gang leader in a series of coordinated attacks involving explosive drones as authorities push to reclaim territory controlled by criminal groups. Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé confirmed the death of Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang operating in the densely populated Cité Soleil neighborhood of Port-au-Prince. “One less gang leader,” Fils-Aimé declared on social media, reaffirming his government's commitment to dismantling the armed groups responsible for widespread violence and instability across Haiti. Saintil's gang is affiliated with the powerful Viv Ansanm coalition, an alliance of armed groups that controls significant portions of the capital and has expanded its influence into other regions of the country. Haitian police said Saintil died from multiple gunshot wounds sustained during a security operation. However, the National Human Rights Defense Network (RNDDH) reported that he was critically injured Thursday night when an explosive drone struck his vehicle and died the following day. According to the human rights organization, at least seven explosive drones were deployed during coordinated operations targeting several gang-controlled communities. The RNDDH reported that five gang members were killed and approximately 15 others injured in the attack targeting Saintil, while additional casualties were recorded during separate confrontations. The operations form part of an intensified campaign by Haitian authorities and international security partners to weaken armed gangs and restore government control over communities affected by years of violence. Security forces have also targeted Wilson Joseph, leader of the notorious 400 Mawozo gang, which has been linked to kidnappings and other violent crimes. Joseph's home was reportedly bombed during a recent operation, although he is believed to have survived the attack and gone into hiding. The latest offensive comes amid an expanded international security presence in Haiti, including the deployment of approximately 2,500 Salvadoran troops following the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians during a gang ambush in October. The technicians went missing on October 18 after armed gangs attacked their vehicle near Port-au-Prince. Haitian police subsequently recovered the burned-out vehicle in the Santo district of Croix-des-Bouquets, but the four men remain missing. The incident has heightened tensions and prompted additional security operations targeting armed groups suspected of involvement in the attack. Meanwhile, the RNDDH has raised concerns about the potential impact of explosive drone operations on civilians living in densely populated neighborhoods. The organization has called attention to reports of civilian casualties as security forces increasingly rely on drone strikes to target gang leaders and their strongholds. Haiti has experienced years of escalating gang violence, with armed groups controlling major roads, neighborhoods and commercial routes, particularly in and around Port-au-Prince. The violence has forced hundreds of thousands of residents to flee their homes, disrupted essential services and severely restricted access to food, healthcare and humanitarian assistance. The latest operations come as Prime Minister Fils-Aimé has identified restoring security and organizing elections as his government's two main priorities. In a recent national address, he pledged that the Haitian state would not surrender territory to armed groups and insisted that security operations would continue until public order and state authority were restored. The prime minister has also emphasized that operations must comply with Haitian law and international human rights obligations. Despite the intensified offensive, questions remain about coordination among Haiti's police, military and international security partners, as well as the effectiveness of drone strikes in reducing gang violence without placing civilians at further risk. Authorities have maintained that their objective is to dismantle criminal networks, regain control of gang-held communities and create the security conditions necessary for Haiti's long-awaited elections. extraction.body: In brief: US presidential envoy Jared Kushner has proposed launching multilateral talks between European nations and Russia on post-war continental security, modeling the framework on the defunct NATO-Russia Council. Kushner has outlined five pillars, including crisis communications and military transparency, if progress is made at the Abu Dhabi trilateral talks on Nov. 10-11. US special presidential envoy Jared Kushner has proposed launching multilateral negotiations between European nations and Russia to design a post-war continental security architecture, modeling the initiative on the defunct NATO- Russia Council, The Washington Post reported. According to a senior official familiar with internal deliberations, Kushner seeks to transition diplomatic engagements into a broader multilateral framework with direct European participation if working-level trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US, and Russia achieve progress in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 . Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Writing in a statement on X, Kushner outlined five primary pillars for the proposed security architecture: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications channels, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability. However, European allied governments and Ukrainian leadership have emphasized that any discussions on continental security architecture must remain strictly conditional on first securing a verified ceasefire and an enforceable peace agreement in Ukraine. Kushner’s proposal looks toward the operational template of the NATO -Russia Council, an institutional body established in 2002 to facilitate security coordination and dialogue between the Western alliance and Moscow . The council’s practical operations were suspended in 2014 following Russia’s illegal military invasion and annexation of Ukraine’s Crimean peninsula and its armed incursions into the Donbas region. Diplomatic sources cited by The Washington Post indicated that the proposed mechanism aims to re-engage Moscow across standing security consultations and structured military transparency. European officials who spoke to The Washington Post affirmed their general openness to future dialogue with Moscow, but stressed that an armistice in Ukraine remains a mandatory prerequisite. “Both tracks are on,” messaged a knowledgeable official from a close US ally. However, the official cautioned: “A Ukraine peace agreement has to be settled before an agreement on security architecture.” A senior official from another key European country noted that while European leaders choose to engage rather than isolate themselves from the diplomatic initiative, European capitals maintain a unified red line regarding sequencing. “Many risks for us in this approach, but better to engage than not,” the senior European official explained. “Our approach is still that these issues can be discussed only after the war… Not gonna be easy talks.” The official added that despite willingness among prominent European heads of state to support Kushner’s diplomatic outreach, “broad unity in Europe” exists around the fundamental principle that an operational ceasefire in Ukraine must precede any Europe-Russia discussions. President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected the notion of prioritizing broader European security talks over an end to hostilities , warning that Moscow’s push to discuss continental structures first is dangerous. Speaking in an interview with CNN host Jake Tapper, Zelensky stated that diplomatic sequencing must place the cessation of the war and binding security guarantees for Ukraine before any multilateral framework involving Russia is evaluated. “The idea of discussing a European-Russian security infrastructure is not simple, and it can be dangerous,” Zelensky said. “I have been very clear with all partners: first, we must discuss how to end Russia’s war against Ukraine. Second, what the security infrastructure for Ukraine will look like. What security guarantees Ukraine will receive.” Zelensky warned that allowing Russia to participate in restructuring continental security while actively striking civilian population centers and energy grids risks repeating historical errors. The president recalled the 1945 Yalta Conference, emphasizing that Ukraine and Europe must avoid a “Yalta 2.0” where great powers negotiate spheres of influence over the heads of sovereign states. extraction.body: In brief: US presidential envoy Jared Kushner has proposed launching multilateral talks between European nations and Russia on post-war continental security, modeling the framework on the defunct NATO-Russia Council. Kushner has outlined five pillars, including crisis communications and military transparency, if progress is made at the Abu Dhabi trilateral talks on Nov. 10-11. US special presidential envoy Jared Kushner has proposed launching multilateral negotiations between European nations and Russia to design a post-war continental security architecture, modeling the initiative on the defunct NATO- Russia Council, The Washington Post reported. According to a senior official familiar with internal deliberations, Kushner seeks to transition diplomatic engagements into a broader multilateral framework with direct European participation if working-level trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US, and Russia achieve progress in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 . Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . Writing in a statement on X, Kushner outlined five primary pillars for the proposed security architecture: permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications channels, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability. However, European allied governments and Ukrainian leadership have emphasized that any discussions on continental security architecture must remain strictly conditional on first securing a verified ceasefire and an enforceable peace agreement in Ukraine. Kushner’s proposal looks toward the operational template of the NATO -Russia Council, an institutional body established in 2002 to facilitate security coordination and dialogue between the Western alliance and Moscow . The council’s practical operations were suspended in 2014 following Russia’s illegal military invasion and annexation of Ukraine’s Crimean peninsula and its armed incursions into the Donbas region. Diplomatic sources cited by The Washington Post indicated that the proposed mechanism aims to re-engage Moscow across standing security consultations and structured military transparency. European officials who spoke to The Washington Post affirmed their general openness to future dialogue with Moscow, but stressed that an armistice in Ukraine remains a mandatory prerequisite. “Both tracks are on,” messaged a knowledgeable official from a close US ally. However, the official cautioned: “A Ukraine peace agreement has to be settled before an agreement on security architecture.” A senior official from another key European country noted that while European leaders choose to engage rather than isolate themselves from the diplomatic initiative, European capitals maintain a unified red line regarding sequencing. “Many risks for us in this approach, but better to engage than not,” the senior European official explained. “Our approach is still that these issues can be discussed only after the war… Not gonna be easy talks.” The official added that despite willingness among prominent European heads of state to support Kushner’s diplomatic outreach, “broad unity in Europe” exists around the fundamental principle that an operational ceasefire in Ukraine must precede any Europe-Russia discussions. President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected the notion of prioritizing broader European security talks over an end to hostilities , warning that Moscow’s push to discuss continental structures first is dangerous. Speaking in an interview with CNN host Jake Tapper, Zelensky stated that diplomatic sequencing must place the cessation of the war and binding security guarantees for Ukraine before any multilateral framework involving Russia is evaluated. “The idea of discussing a European-Russian security infrastructure is not simple, and it can be dangerous,” Zelensky said. “I have been very clear with all partners: first, we must discuss how to end Russia’s war against Ukraine. Second, what the security infrastructure for Ukraine will look like. What security guarantees Ukraine will receive.” Zelensky warned that allowing Russia to participate in restructuring continental security while actively striking civilian population centers and energy grids risks repeating historical errors. The president recalled the 1945 Yalta Conference, emphasizing that Ukraine and Europe must avoid a “Yalta 2.0” where great powers negotiate spheres of influence over the heads of sovereign states. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a gold mine for companies selling chips and building data centers . But without software, those AI chips don't really have anything to do. That's why I think software stocks are as important as chipmakers and hyperscalers when you consider how to invest in the AI build-out. The more companies depend on AI, the more important those software services become. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Two companies that stand to benefit are Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD). They approach AI from different directions, but both are already seeing growing demand for their products. With $5,000 to invest, I'd consider splitting my money equally between these two outstanding software stocks. You likely already use Microsoft software, though you may not realize it. Microsoft makes some of the most popular software programs, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. All of them are available in the company's popular Microsoft 365 suite. In addition, its Azure cloud platform supplies the infrastructure needed to develop and run AI applications. Azure AI Foundry provides tools for developers to build those applications, while GitHub Copilot helps them write code. The strategy is paying off. In Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended Sept. 30, Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 48% year over year to $33.16 billion. Microsoft has also incorporated Copilot in its 365 software suite of office tools. During the quarter, Microsoft reported that daily Copilot users increased nearly 50% sequentially and more than fivefold year over year. The number of customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats also increased more than eightfold year over year. That's particularly encouraging because it demonstrates that businesses are willing to pay for AI capabilities within software they already use. Microsoft reported $677 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations, representing contracted revenue that hasn't yet been recognized. That figure increased 73% year over year, although commitments from OpenAI contributed substantially to the growth. If there's a downside to Microsoft stock now, however, it's in spending. Microsoft is dropping billions of dollars every quarter to satisfy AI demand. Capital expenditures reached $45.2 billion in the quarter, and management expects spending to increase to $50 billion in Q2. Those investments are putting pressure on margins, and there's no guarantee they'll produce the returns investors expect. Still, Microsoft generated $18.6 billion in quarterly free cash flow despite its spending. That gives the company considerable financial flexibility as it expands its AI business. While AI offers businesses new opportunities to develop new products and work more efficiently, it also creates new opportunities for cybercriminals. And unfortunately, there are always bad actors looking for an opportunity to break the rules and make a quick buck. Companies that deploy AI agents capable of accessing sensitive information and performing tasks without constant human supervision are susceptible to cyberattacks, and CrowdStrike addresses these risks through its Falcon cybersecurity platform. During the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings call, CEO George Kurtz discussed the emerging market for AI detection and response (AIDR). He suggested that protecting AI agents could eventually become a larger business than traditional endpoint detection and response. That's an ambitious prediction, but CrowdStrike's existing business is already producing impressive results. In the quarter ended July 31, revenue increased 26% year over year to $1.47 billion. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $5.84 billion, up 25%, while net new ARR jumped 51% to a record $333 million. And there's evidence that customers are expanding their relationships with CrowdStrike. The company reported that ARR from accounts adopting its Falcon Flex subscription model exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101% from the previous year. Falcon Flex allows customers to adopt additional security products under a flexible purchasing arrangement. So, CrowdStrike doesn't have to rely exclusively on finding new customers. It can generate additional revenue by selling more services to businesses already using its platform. extraction.body: Chips get the headlines, but Microsoft and CrowdStrike sell the software that puts AI to work and keeps it secure. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been a gold mine for companies selling chips and building data centers . But without software, those AI chips don't really have anything to do. That's why I think software stocks are as important as chipmakers and hyperscalers when you consider how to invest in the AI build-out. The more companies depend on AI, the more important those software services become. Two companies that stand to benefit are Microsoft ( MSFT -0.99% ) and CrowdStrike ( CRWD -0.14% ) . They approach AI from different directions, but both are already seeing growing demand for their products. With $5,000 to invest, I'd consider splitting my money equally between these two outstanding software stocks. You likely already use Microsoft software, though you may not realize it. Microsoft makes some of the most popular software programs, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. All of them are available in the company's popular Microsoft 365 suite. In addition, its Azure cloud platform supplies the infrastructure needed to develop and run AI applications. Azure AI Foundry provides tools for developers to build those applications, while GitHub Copilot helps them write code. The strategy is paying off. In Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended Sept. 30, Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 48% year over year to $33.16 billion. Microsoft has also incorporated Copilot in its 365 software suite of office tools. During the quarter, Microsoft reported that daily Copilot users increased nearly 50% sequentially and more than fivefold year over year. The number of customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats also increased more than eightfold year over year. That's particularly encouraging because it demonstrates that businesses are willing to pay for AI capabilities within software they already use. Microsoft reported $677 billion in commercial remaining performance obligations, representing contracted revenue that hasn't yet been recognized. That figure increased 73% year over year, although commitments from OpenAI contributed substantially to the growth. If there's a downside to Microsoft stock now, however, it's in spending. Microsoft is dropping billions of dollars every quarter to satisfy AI demand. Capital expenditures reached $45.2 billion in the quarter, and management expects spending to increase to $50 billion in Q2. Those investments are putting pressure on margins, and there's no guarantee they'll produce the returns investors expect. Still, Microsoft generated $18.6 billion in quarterly free cash flow despite its spending. That gives the company considerable financial flexibility as it expands its AI business. While AI offers businesses new opportunities to develop new products and work more efficiently, it also creates new opportunities for cybercriminals. And unfortunately, there are always bad actors looking for an opportunity to break the rules and make a quick buck. Companies that deploy AI agents capable of accessing sensitive information and performing tasks without constant human supervision are susceptible to cyberattacks, and CrowdStrike addresses these risks through its Falcon cybersecurity platform. During the company's fiscal second-quarter earnings call, CEO George Kurtz discussed the emerging market for AI detection and response (AIDR). He suggested that protecting AI agents could eventually become a larger business than traditional endpoint detection and response. That's an ambitious prediction, but CrowdStrike's existing business is already producing impressive results. In the quarter ended July 31, revenue increased 26% year over year to $1.47 billion. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) reached $5.84 billion, up 25%, while net new ARR jumped 51% to a record $333 million. And there's evidence that customers are expanding their relationships with CrowdStrike . The company reported that ARR from accounts adopting its Falcon Flex subscription model exceeded $2.29 billion, up 101% from the previous year. Falcon Flex allows customers to adopt additional security products under a flexible purchasing arrangement. Both have demonstrated that customers are willing to pay for their services. For long-term investors, that's a more compelling argument than simply betting that AI will continue to grow. Patrick Sanders has no position in any of the stocks mentioned. sources.title: Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses — investigation reveals businesses have ties to sanctioned Chinese military suppliers - Tom's Hardware
passages: An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them.

According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.
President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors.
The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China .
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra.
The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.
Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links.
It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.

An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military. This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication. Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE , which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces. The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military. Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has b lacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are. Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center. President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China . Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones. An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.

This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication.

Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE , which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.

The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military.

Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has b lacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are.

Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.

President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China . Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones.

story.title: Two Chinese companies cleared to buy banned Nvidia AI chips have empty offices and unknown addresses — investigation reveals businesses have ties to sanctioned Chinese military suppliers - Tom's Hardware

facts.text: An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them.

According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.
President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors.
The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China .
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra.
The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.
Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links.
It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.

An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military. This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication. Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE , which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces. The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military. Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has b lacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are. Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center. President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China . Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones. An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them. According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.

This news has revealed concerns that the U.S. Department of Commerce is simply rubber-stamping GPU export license applications instead of scrutinizing each one for potential links to Beijing. “I have a ton of concerns that neither the Commerce Department or Nvidia is doing the due diligence needed to ensure that the licensing terms are being followed,” former China director for the White House National Security Council Liza Tobin told the publication.

Many of these approved companies include well-known entities like Baidu, BYD, Tesla Shanghai, as well as ZTE , which has previously been blacklisted from the U.S. market, Alibaba, Tencent, and ByteDance. However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra. The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.

The New Matrix website also reportedly did not contain any information about its owners or its history, although public company records reveal that it was founded by Li Bin, who, along with two other primary owners, are connected to Wise Road, a Chinese private equity firm sanctioned by the U.S. for helping Beijing acquire sensitive chip technologies. Furthermore, Mr. Li chairs Tsinghua Unigroup, a tech conglomerate partly owned by the Chinese government, and owns New H3C Semiconductor Technologies, which has also been added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List for cooperating with the Chinese military.

Maginfra, on the other hand, is suspected of being linked to Inspur, which Washington has b lacklisted since 2023 for supporting the People’s Liberation Army, with both companies sharing personnel, patents, and a similar government ownership structure. These two firms aren’t listed as the final users of Nvidia’s AI chips, though. Instead, they’re supposed to assemble them into AI servers, which would then be forwarded to a final user, although it’s unclear who their customers are.

Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links. Zhejiang Yindun Cloud Technology’s executives are reportedly related to the founder of Range Intelligent Computing Technology Group, a data center operator that has sold compute capacity to Chinese military contractors. It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.

President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors. The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China . Beijing’s refusal to give Chinese tech companies the green light to buy the chips for the first few months of the year caused the delay. But once China lifted its import ban on Nvidia chips, several Chinese companies applied for licenses to buy them, and The New York Times reported that around two dozen firms have already received approval, including these questionable ones.

coreFacts.text: An investigation has found that addresses for two Chinese companies approved to purchase Nvidia H200 chips led to empty offices, and the receptionists at the buildings were unfamiliar with them.

According to The New York Times , these companies didn’t just have empty offices; their executives are often linked to other firms sanctioned by the United States for working with and providing advanced technology to the Chinese military.
President Donald Trump banned the export of Nvidia AI GPUs in April 2025 , even those customized to meet the performance ceiling Washington set for AI processors.
The president reversed the decision late last year in exchange for a 25% cut of the sale, but it still took more than eight months for the first H200 shipments to arrive in China .
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
However, the outfit’s investigation also revealed approval for two relatively unknown firms: New Matrix and Maginfra.
The offices for both companies were empty shells with some office furniture, and people working nearby said they’d never heard of the company or seen anyone go to the deserted spaces.
Aside from these questionable non-entities, another company that received a license to purchase H200 GPUs has some suspicious links.
It’s also reportedly partly operating out of a Range data center.

sources.title: The Duo apps are coming, says Apple - TechCrunch
passages: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch.
But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front.

The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year.
On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve .
The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added.
Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo.
However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon.

extraction.body: The early iPhone Duo reviews were a bit hard on Apple’s new foldable for the lack of Duo-optimized apps available at the time of launch. But Apple says things are changing quickly on the software front. The company on Friday announced there are now over 100,000 apps built for the Duo live on the App Store, and it’s seeing thousands more being added to the store every day. The news was timed alongside the release of over a dozen more notable Duo-ready apps, including Microsoft Word and Outlook, Zoom, sports apps from the NBA and NHL, shopping apps like Etsy and LTK, productivity apps like Goodnotes and Extra, the Halide Mark III camera app, and others. These join the iPhone Duo-optimized apps that were already available, like Netflix, YouTube, Instagram, and WhatsApp. Non-optimized apps are definitely less than ideal, as they come with a black bar on the side of the screen, which takes up valuable space. Sometimes, they hide important functions under an overflow menu. Apple’s data seems to suggest that at least some iOS developers may have needed extra time to get their apps ready for its latest form factor. The company said that more than 2,000 app developers attended its over 50 in-person workshops that were hosted across 19 cities worldwide. Here, the developers could use the Duo and work on their apps with Apple’s support. The Duo has also proven to be more popular than perhaps Apple had planned for, given its high price point. (It starts at $1,999 for the 256GB model.) The device quickly sold out within hours of orders opening up, and now, Duo ship times have shifted into the next year. On its earnings call this week, Apple said it’s “hard to predict” when the Duo constraints leading to those delays will improve . “It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” said Susan Prescott, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Developer Relations, in a statement referring to the 100,000-app milestone. “The enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo,” she added. Other notable apps that have been updated for iOS 27 and optimized for the iPhone Duo include the following: Spotify, CBS, Tubi, BBC iPlayer (U.K.), Yahoo Fantasy Sports, Sportsnet (Canada), Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, ChatGPT, Grok Bot, Microsoft Copilot, Excel, PowerPoint, SAP Concur, monday.com, PDF Expert, Documents, iA Writer, Substack, The Washington Post, Yahoo News, FOX News, Kalshi, Yahoo Finance, Canva, Suno, Tinder, Google Translate, Strava, Alma, Withings, MyFitnessPal, Bevel, Transit, Citi Bike, ParkMobile, Viator, Tesla Robotaxi, Priceline, Kroger, Domino’s, Taco Bell, Untappd, The Weather Channel, FOX Weather, and RainViewer. Not all these updates have yet to fully roll out, we should note. Spotify, for instance, is still showing the black bar on the side, and the App Store doesn’t yet say an update is available on our review unit of the Duo. However, given that this list comes directly from Apple, we expect to see these updates soon. The company’s AR glasses — which the company calls a “new kind of computer” — were heavy (they weighed around 8 ounces) and fit rather uncomfortably on my face.
The device was also hot, and made my face feel tingly — a common side-effect of smart glasses where massive computing is happening under the hood.
Specs now comes in two sizes — 47mm and 52mm.
They also now come equipped with spring hinges, which make the device more flexible and comfortable.
Fast forward to late October, when I met back up with the Snap team at a Four Seasons in downtown San Francisco.
It’s an interesting product that — like a lot of its peers — doesn’t necessarily seem to have a clear purpose but, in time, could become many things.

What I can say is this: Specs has improved the form factor significantly since my first brush with the device.
